# Microsoft Azure Data Box Edge management client library for .NET

Microsoft Azure Data Box Edge is a physical network appliance, shipped by Microsoft, that sends data in and out of Azure. Data Box Edge is additionally equipped with AI-enabled edge computing capabilities that help you analyze, process, and transform the on-premises data before uploading it to the cloud.

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Data Box Edge resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Data Box Edge management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.DataBoxEdge
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions

proposals.subtype: Obsolete device-capacity operation stubs
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete sync/async GetDeviceCapacityInfo methods immediately throw NotSupportedException and direct callers to a capacity-info subresource API. Neither performs a request or returns capacity data; the Task-returning form is not declared async.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom explicitly implements the deprecated signatures and throwing bodies outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete network-settings operation stubs
proposals.explanation: GetNetworkSettings and GetNetworkSettingsAsync are hidden, obsolete and unconditionally throw with replacement subresource guidance. They do not adapt or retrieve network settings at runtime, including in the non-async Task-returning form.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Explicit obsolete throwing methods are supplied by the Custom resource partial.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete update-summary operation stubs
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete GetUpdateSummary sync/async pair contains only immediate NotSupportedException throws naming a replacement subresource API. No update-summary HTTP operation, polling or result conversion is implemented here.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom contains the explicit deprecated public signatures and nonfunctional bodies.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete capacity-model factory stub
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete DataBoxEdgeDeviceCapacityInfo factory accepts resource metadata and capacity fields but only throws, directing callers to DataBoxEdgeDeviceCapacityInfoData. It constructs no model.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom factory explicitly preserves a deprecated signature through an unconditional throw.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete network-settings factory stub
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete DataBoxEdgeDeviceNetworkSettings factory takes resource metadata/networkAdapters but immediately throws with replacement Data-suffixed factory guidance. There is no collection normalization or model construction in its body.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom supplies the explicit obsolete factory signature and throwing implementation.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete update-summary factory stub
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete DataBoxEdgeDeviceUpdateSummary factory accepts the listed resource/update fields but only throws NotSupportedException, recommending DataBoxEdgeDeviceUpdateSummaryData. No update model or serialization result is produced.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A Custom partial contains the explicit deprecated factory signature and throw rather than a functioning generated factory.

proposals.subtype: Nullable bandwidth factory constructing nested properties with guarded omission
proposals.explanation: The nullable factory constructs BandwidthScheduleData with no properties when startOn, stopOn, rateInMbps and days are all null. Otherwise it constructs BandwidthScheduleProperties, dereferences all three nullable scalars, materializes days with an empty-list fallback and passes null additional data. Supplying only some inputs can therefore dereference an absent scalar; the guard is all-null, not per-field validation.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom implements explicit nested-properties construction and collection conversion outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Nullable share factory assembling properties and materializing rights/mappings
proposals.explanation: The nullable share factory omits ShareProperties only when every listed property input is null. Otherwise it builds the nested model, reads shareStatus.Value, monitoringStatus.Value and accessProtocol.Value, converts three collection inputs to lists with empty fallbacks and forwards the remaining values. A partial argument set can enter this branch with a dereferenced enum still null.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated Custom factory explicitly assembles nested properties and collection representations.

proposals.subtype: Nullable storage-credential factory assembling a nested properties model
proposals.explanation: The factory passes null properties when all credential inputs are null; otherwise it builds StorageAccountCredentialProperties from alias, username, encrypted key, connection string, SSL status, domain, account type and storage account ID. sslStatus.Value and accountType.Value are read in that branch even if another supplied input alone triggered construction.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom contains concrete property-bag construction and nullable-to-value conversions rather than an authentication implementation.

proposals.subtype: Nullable storage-account factory assembling nested properties
proposals.explanation: The factory omits StorageAccountProperties only when all six property inputs are null. Otherwise it forwards description, nullable storage status, credential ID, endpoint and count while reading dataPolicy.Value. Other non-null inputs can select that branch with dataPolicy absent.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom factory explicitly constructs the nested properties and adapts a nullable enum to its value.

proposals.subtype: Nullable container factory constructing properties with a required dereference
proposals.explanation: The factory passes null ContainerProperties when containerStatus, dataFormat, refreshDetails and createdOn are all absent. Otherwise it constructs that model using dataFormat.Value and the remaining nullable/reference inputs. A non-null status, refresh detail or timestamp alone can expose a missing dataFormat dereference.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated Custom factory supplies explicit conditional construction and nullable enum conversion.

proposals.subtype: Nullable user factory materializing share rights into nested properties
proposals.explanation: The factory omits UserProperties when encryptedPassword, shareAccessRights and userType are all null. Otherwise it materializes rights with an empty tracked-list fallback, forwards the encrypted password and reads userType.Value. Password or rights supplied without userType can reach an absent-value dereference.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom explicitly implements collection normalization and nested model construction outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Nullable diagnostic-consent factory conditionally creating properties
proposals.explanation: The factory builds DiagnosticProactiveLogCollectionSettingData with null nested properties when userConsent is null, otherwise creates ProactiveLogCollectionSettingsProperties(userConsent.Value,null). Unlike the multi-input factories, this conditional guards the same nullable value it dereferences.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom factory explicitly supplies conditional nested-model construction outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Nullable Arc-addon factory selecting a discriminator and assembling properties
proposals.explanation: The factory fixes AddonType.ArcForKubernetes and null additional data. It omits ArcAddonProperties when all eight addon inputs are absent; otherwise it constructs them using resourceLocation.Value and the other supplied values. Supplying another addon field without location can trigger an absent-value dereference.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom factory explicitly selects the discriminator and conditionally assembles a nested properties model.

proposals.subtype: Hidden bandwidth factory converting required scalars to nullable arguments
proposals.explanation: The hidden overload casts startOn, stopOn and rateInMbps to nullable types and forwards all arguments to the supplied nullable BandwidthScheduleData factory.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom explicitly implements a hidden overload and typed argument conversions.

proposals.subtype: Hidden share factory converting required enum arguments to nullable types
proposals.explanation: The hidden share overload casts shareStatus, monitoringStatus and accessProtocol to their nullable counterparts and forwards the other values and collections unchanged to the supplied nullable factory.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom partial explicitly implements hidden signature adaptation rather than constructing another independent model.

proposals.subtype: Hidden storage-credential factory converting enum arguments
proposals.explanation: The hidden overload casts sslStatus and accountType to nullable types and forwards all other credential/resource arguments to the supplied nullable factory. It implements no credential authentication or encryption.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Concrete hidden forwarding and nullable casts are supplied in Custom.

proposals.subtype: Hidden storage-account factory converting the data-policy argument
proposals.explanation: The hidden overload casts the nonnullable dataPolicy to DataBoxEdgeDataPolicy? and forwards the remaining inputs to the supplied nullable factory.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom explicitly implements this hidden signature adapter.

proposals.subtype: Hidden container factory converting the data-format argument
proposals.explanation: The hidden overload converts dataFormat to DataBoxEdgeStorageContainerDataFormat? and delegates all arguments to the supplied nullable storage-container factory.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: An explicit hidden overload and typed cast are implemented in Custom.

proposals.subtype: Hidden user factory converting the user-type argument
proposals.explanation: The hidden overload casts userType to DataBoxEdgeUserType? and forwards encryptedPassword, shareAccessRights and resource metadata to the supplied nullable factory.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom partial supplies explicit hidden forwarding and argument conversion.

proposals.subtype: Hidden diagnostic-consent factory converting a required enum
proposals.explanation: The hidden diagnostic settings overload casts userConsent to ProactiveDiagnosticsConsent? and delegates with the unchanged resource metadata to the supplied nullable factory.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom explicitly implements this hidden typed overload adapter.

proposals.subtype: Hidden Arc-addon factory converting the resource location
proposals.explanation: The hidden EdgeArcAddon overload casts resourceLocation to AzureLocation? and forwards the other addon/resource arguments to the supplied nullable factory.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom factory contains an explicit hidden signature adapter with a typed location conversion.

proposals.subtype: Deprecated capacity-info model shape with unsupported access and JSON interfaces
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete DataBoxEdgeDeviceCapacityInfo type derives from ResourceData and declares a public empty constructor. Its four declared capacity properties and all supplied JSON/persistence method bodies throw NotSupportedException. The constructor itself does not throw; this supplies a type shape, not usable capacity state or a functioning JSON codec.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom explicitly declares the obsolete replacement model shape and nonfunctional property/interface bodies.

proposals.subtype: Deprecated network-settings type with unsupported state and JSON interfaces
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete DataBoxEdgeDeviceNetworkSettings ResourceData subtype has an empty public constructor, a throwing NetworkAdapters getter and throwing JSON/persistence implementations. It exposes a declared model shape but does not implement network state access or serialization.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete supplied Custom model declaration explicitly implements deprecated shape-preserving stubs.

proposals.subtype: Deprecated update-summary type with throwing declared members
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete DataBoxEdgeDeviceUpdateSummary ResourceData subtype has an empty public constructor. All its supplied update-version/status/count/job/list property accessors and JSON/persistence bodies throw NotSupportedException. This is one nonfunctional replacement type shape, not independent implementations of update operations, LROs or serialization.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom explicitly provides the deprecated model declaration and throwing state/interface members outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Hidden parameterless role-addon constructor forwarding default
proposals.explanation: The public hidden DataBoxEdgeRoleAddonData() constructor delegates to this(default). The target constructor signature/type and body are absent, so the default argument's concrete value and generated discriminator handling are not inferred.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom partial supplies a substantive constructor initializer despite its empty body.

proposals.subtype: Hidden parameterless role constructor forwarding default
proposals.explanation: The public hidden DataBoxEdgeRoleData() constructor delegates to this(default). Comments describe an earlier parameterless baseline and a new discriminator parameter, but no target implementation or historical baseline is supplied to verify that account.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Custom implements an explicit public hidden constructor initializer outside Generated.

decisions.reason: Both handwritten resource methods are obsolete, hidden, and immediately throw; the cited lines support an unsupported legacy API shim, not a functioning retrieval wrapper.
The cited sync/Task-returning network-settings methods retain signatures but immediately throw, with obsolete replacement guidance.
The update-summary method pair is handwritten, hidden, obsolete, and unconditionally throws rather than fetching update data.
The non-generated factory declares the obsolete capacity-info signature but its entire implementation is a NotSupportedException with replacement guidance.
The network-settings factory stub is hidden, obsolete and throwing, preserving a distinct deprecated factory entry point without constructing a model.
The update-summary factory has a handwritten legacy signature and immediate throw; its numerous parameters are not used to construct a model.
The factory's non-generated implementation conditionally constructs nested bandwidth properties, dereferences nullable values and materializes days; its all-null guard does not guard each scalar.
The handwritten share factory builds nested properties, dereferences nullable enums and materializes three collection arguments; cited lines substantiate the stated conditional behavior.
The credential factory conditionally assembles a nested model and reads nullable enum Value members without an individual null guard; it does not implement authentication.
The storage-account factory uses an all-null properties guard and reads dataPolicy.Value in its construction branch; this is handwritten model factory behavior.
The container factory conditionally constructs ContainerProperties and dereferences dataFormat.Value when any property input is present, matching the cited source.
The user factory materializes share rights and reads userType.Value inside an all-null-guarded nested-properties branch; the behavior is implemented outside Generated.
The diagnostic factory creates nested properties only when the same nullable consent it dereferences is non-null; the concrete source supports a model factory method.
The non-generated Arc addon factory passes a fixed discriminator and conditionally creates properties with resourceLocation.Value; a different present field can select that branch.
The hidden nonnullable bandwidth overload casts three values and delegates to the nullable overload, preserving a distinct factory signature.
The hidden share overload forwards to its nullable counterpart with explicit nullable enum casts; it is a signature adapter rather than another model construction.
The credential factory overload only adapts two enum arguments and forwards to its nullable counterpart, as the cited lines show.
The hidden storage-account overload preserves a nonnullable policy parameter by casting and forwarding to the nullable factory.
The container overload supplies a hidden nonnullable format signature and forwards with a nullable format cast.
The user factory overload explicitly casts the nonnullable user type and delegates to the nullable signature.
The hidden diagnostic factory overload casts consent to its nullable type and delegates without adding another diagnostic implementation.
The hidden Arc addon overload casts the nonnullable location and forwards to its nullable factory, supplying a separate compatibility signature.
The custom obsolete type has an empty constructor, throwing property accessors and throwing model serialization members; this is one retained, unusable model shape, not working serialization.
The custom obsolete network-settings model preserves a declared type and property but throws on access and on JSON/persistence methods; it is not a functioning network model.
The deprecated custom update-summary model declares many members, all with throwing accessors or serialization implementations; one retained model shape covers that behavior.
A public parameterless constructor is handwritten outside Generated, hidden from IntelliSense and delegates through this(default); no target implementation is assumed.
The handwritten role constructor is public, hidden and forwards a default argument; the source does not establish the target constructor's implementation or historical baseline.

limitations: Seven Custom files of 527 eligible files were captured; four named Custom files were skipped. Findings do not constitute an exhaustive package inventory.

Comments describe AutoRest-to-TypeSpec migration, earlier API baselines, generator suppression/nullability comparison rules and replacement subresources. Those historical/generator accounts are not independently verified by the supplied generated counterparts, compiler/emitter source or old API files.

Seven multi-input nullable factory implementations can select nested construction while a .Value operand remains null. Their generator addressability is unclear because the intended relationship between nullable public inputs and required nested values is not established. This observation is part of each factory finding, not a separately counted bug or an implemented fix.

The diagnostic-consent factory guards the same nullable value it dereferences; its behavior is distinguished from the seven multi-input cases. Hidden nonnullable forwarders provide typed casts and are separate signature-adaptation behaviors from the constructing overloads.

Each obsolete model is grouped as one type-shape stub, including its declared throwing accessors/interface methods. The public empty constructor is not described as throwing, inherited ResourceData behavior is unknown, and these bodies are not functioning custom serialization.
Throwing operation and factory families remain distinct. Task-returning device stubs are not async and throw directly rather than returning working operations or successful task results.

No target constructor, generated serializer or replacement subresource implementation is supplied. Generator-addressable yes means a plausible emission shape, not demonstrated support, and none of these findings establishes custom LRO polling or an authentication algorithm.
The request captured only seven files from 527 eligible files, with four specifically skipped for review budget; decisions do not establish exhaustive customization discovery or absence elsewhere.

Generated source, prior API baseline and target constructor implementations are not supplied. Historical and generator-behavior assertions in source comments are not independently verified; judgments rely on the visible handwritten bodies and signatures.

Factory overloads are assessed by their distinct callable signatures and implementations within the captured source; whether a generator would otherwise have emitted identical nested construction cannot be verified from these excerpts.
Accepted here means AI-reviewed on the supplied evidence, not human-verified.
